title: Build contracts: the commit act and file_claim (design T-436), no windows or damages yet
description: Decisions 2 (2026-10-08) and 3 (2026-10-21) ratified; construction waited on identity tokens, which T-446 and T-454 delivered. The three numbers are not ratified yet (decision 10), so nothing time- or amount-based is built here.
acceptance_criteria: attest.py gains the unprivileged kinds commit (T-436 section 1), answer (T-452 section 2) and appeal (T-452 section 5). None joins PRIVILEGED_KINDS; a test pins that set unchanged.

A commit act is self-filed by the committing name, requires a task, and records exactly one operational parameter from PR-060 clause 1's list with its committed value, as T-436 section 1 specifies. A parameter outside that list is refused.

file_claim as T-436 section 5 specifies it, with a CLI verb: it reads the respondent's commit act and the one named independent source. When the values agree it refuses and writes nothing anywhere: no act, no event line, no file, proved by hashing acts/ and the event log before and after. When they disagree it signs one contest act on the CLAIMANT's own chain naming the respondent, the commit act's digest, the observed source and the gap.

Tests also cover: a commit reference that is not on the respondent's own chain is refused; a true gap files exactly one act. The raw contest verb stays callable directly (the BYPASS residual T-436 names as open); a test pins that it still writes, so nobody reads it as closed.
Nothing computes a deadline, a window, a lapse, a debit or a damages amount: those wait for decision 10. Nothing reads reputation; a PR-022 clause 4 output-shape guard pins it.
Edit attest.py and tests only; precedent.py belongs to T-468. Do not edit CLAUDE.md. The suite passes via goal_mode. Hand off to verifier.

Acceptance criteria walkthrough:
1. commit/answer/appeal added, unprivileged; PRIVILEGED_KINDS pinned unchanged by test (frozenset({"verdict","contest","distinguish","grant"})).
2. commit() requires --task, requires parameter in OPERATIONAL_PARAMETERS={task,order,budget,deadline,engine,iteration_bound} (PR-060 clause1's six), refuses any other parameter and a blank value; records exactly one {parameter,value} pair in the act body.
3. file_claim() CLI verb `file-claim`: reads respondent's commit act by seq (verifies it is kind=commit and signature-verifies under the respondent's own key), compares to --observed-value/--source; agreement raises AttestError and writes nothing -- proven in FileClaimOutcomeA by hashing acts/+events.jsonl before/after the call (byte-identical); disagreement calls contest() (kind=contest) naming the respondent, the commit digest, observed value/source and the gap in the contest act's `reason` field.
4. Tests: seq not on respondent's own chain -> refused ("no act at seq"); non-commit-kind act referenced -> refused; true gap -> exactly one act filed (asserted via acts_on() count delta); raw `contest` CLI verb still writes unconditionally even with no real gap (TheRawContestVerbStillWrites) -- pinned open, not closed.
5. Nothing in commit/answer/appeal/file_claim computes a deadline/window/lapse/debit/damages amount -- AST guard (OutputShapeGuard) asserts no BinOp and no ordering comparison (<,>,<=,>=) anywhere in those four function bodies, plus a forbidden-identifier scan (reputation, standing, debit, damages_amount, lapse_at, objection_deadline); both guards carry a planted-violation negative control proving they can actually catch a regression, mirroring test_attest_retraction.py's own discipline.
6. Edited only .harness/bin/attest.py and added .harness/tests/test_attest_contracts.py; did not touch precedent.py (T-468's) or CLUADE.md.

File_claim's held-kinds inheritance is exercised directly: a delegate granted only `verdict` (never `contest`) gets sign_act's own "DELEGATION CEILING: ... cannot sign a 'contest' act" message unchanged, proving Outcome B adds no shortcut and no bespoke refusal text.
